poems/a-beautiful-curse.html.title: A Beautiful Curse
poems/a-beautiful-curse.html.subtitle: An oak tree. Unanticipated rain. A love that only blooms in verse.
poems/a-beautiful-curse.html.html:
I

A beautiful autumn night sky

Enveloped a rather desolating

Conversation which seemed shy

While a nightingale was in hiding.

◆
II

An oak tree on top of a hill

Had leaves of colour blue

That fell & left a trail in shrill

While a chilly & cold wind blew.

◆
III

The changes in the seasons

Made her nonchalantly smile

& they faded swiftly with treasons

Of my past, that still hide in a lie.

◆
IV

A glimmer of lightning fazed

Us as we stood in the shade

Of an oak tree that was hazed

By the autumn's lie in charade.

◆
V

Unanticipated rain poured

On my already anxious heart

And on the tree that ignored

This life which has kept us apart.

◆
VI

I never tended to care about

The seasonal changes around me

But when I read a poem in doubt

My love for her bloomed like a lily.

◆
VII

Various seasons had passed

And in grief we diverged our path

While only memories could last

As now I sit under a shed of lath.

◆
VIII

This thin shed hasn't provided

Shade from the rain as I write

About a love that has subsided

As I await a nostalgic night.

◆
IX

I stumbled upon the old oak tree

Whose blue leaves fall in autumn

This night sky frees me from misery

And a memory seeps in my poetry.

◆
X

Poetry that alludes me everyday

Has been about a seasonal woman

That dances by a garden where I lay

Dreaming under the oak tree, in autumn.

poems/a-rainy-day-of-july.html.title: A Rainy Day of July
poems/a-rainy-day-of-july.html.subtitle: Met on a rainy day of July — left on a day of autumn.
poems/a-rainy-day-of-july.html.html:
I

Did I ever wryly abide

To her nostalgic smile

That still lingers on this fray

That I wore on a rainy day.

◆
II

I saw a shocking reflection

By a puddle's misdirection

While I picked the fine rose

Laying beside my damp toes.

◆
III

It was a rainy day of July

When I met a woman so shy,

She had an umbrella that was blue

And a chilly wind had just blew.

◆
IV

Beauty personified her eyes

That made me conjure lies

About myself and the poem

That I read & write in tandem.

◆
V

My love was like a seagull

That crashed in a death fatal,

Yet she was the only twilight

That kindled the sparks inside.

◆
VI

I left her on a day of autumn

That I may regret often

As my love for her was hopeless

While she made me breathless.

◆
VII

Could it be luck or fate

To meet her on this lane

After many sorrowful seasons

That made me commit treasons.

◆
VIII

Treasons are the lines of poetry

Which I find along with this diary

That has her caged with grace

Like a flower in a rainy place.

◆
IX

It seems my love for her

Still sends the same shiver

That makes me want to cry

Like it was a rainy day of July.

poems/a-ring-in-the-rain.html.title: A Ring in the Rain
poems/a-ring-in-the-rain.html.subtitle: Love seen through a curtain of rain.
poems/a-ring-in-the-rain.html.html:
I

While I walk under these lush green trees

that were blessed with rain

they make me perceive an emotion

that resembles my pain.

◆
II

Sometimes I feel like crying

without any idea or reason

even the clouds shower with rain

on this world filled with treason.

◆
III

As I stroll beside these lonely streams

I realised how the world changed

while time flows as it seems

with clusters of emotions left stranded.

◆
IV

I sit on the banks of this deserted river

I notice how the slight drizzle of the rain

and the cold breeze makes me shiver

even the muffler she had given hadn't softened the pain.

◆
V

I look upon this rain

which drenches me in anguish,

I wonder if it could for once, fain

and I grin, for my nostalgic wish.

◆
VI

During the ending of one summer

I had fallen in love too bold

now comes a summer that reminds me of her

and of a love which once was new but now has grown old.

◆
VII

A heartsick smile appeared on my face

as I sauntered among the rain in autumn

I found a place to sit under this shade

a place that I had forgotten

◆
VIII

I walked up to it where I saw pieces of mozzarella

just to find her sitting there

with her hands gripping a blue umbrella

a serene silence engulfed the lair.

◆
IX

I saw the ring on her finger

an anguish filled my mind

I felt a grief that still seemed to linger

while the rain hid my tears in hindsight.

◆
X

Her hair had seemed to have grown longer

while she seemed so glad to see me

I just smiled and waited for a harbinger

who could be the one to hear my plea.

◆
XI

I recalled the scars that she once left plentiful

she still is the woman whom I can't forget

I saw her again and it feels like a curse too beautiful

and she comes anchored with a love in regret.

◆
XII

I bleed through my fingers

that were once gruesomely rough

now I walk away from a love that shivers

a love that has tortured me long enough.

poems/a-wandering-taxi.html.title: A Wandering Taxi
poems/a-wandering-taxi.html.subtitle: The city at midnight.
poems/a-wandering-taxi.html.html:
A wandering taxi stopped in the corner of my street, I sat inside and told him to drive till dawn. His dejected face and his eyes made me realise that we both were wanderers that were just waiting for their moment to drown.

Dawdles, the midnight.

Lonely streets vanish in the wind as the taxi moves, leaving us with lonely faces, lonely hearts and some remorseful memories. While the taxi swerves through the city, tears fall down my face as I reminisce a time when my heart had an empty room, before she barged in and filled it with a wound deep enough.

Lingers on, this wound.

I fell in love with her the day I met her, it felt tragic as I couldn't keep my eyes off her. I saw her in class, seated beside a guy, holding hands with him while my pen fell in disbelief as I could see my fate recur.

Dawdles on, your memory.

Questioning the cruelty of my fate, I spent my days in absolute misery. How could it be that one day life is bliss and the next day, a regretful mockery.

Laughs, my fate.

Being her friend somedays felt joyful but often it was a saddening anecdote which on every recollection, became darker. My heart desired to stay beside her even if it didn't mount to anything yet it was a torture to be someone of no significance to her.

Dithers on, my desire.

My heart thought of her as someone that it could have but never keep. It felt like a sin, to have feelings for her when it wouldn't reach her even if it had taken a faithful leap.

Loiters on, my sin.

When this heart had realised the truth, life swept through in a blur. She is about to be married today and this heart can just hum a saddening melody to soothe my soul until one day, the sun shines brighter.

I cling onto, my heart's lie.

The taxi stops at the same place I boarded it from. Faint sunshine seeps through my coat and this cold as I walk to the coffee shop where I first saw those brown eyes and fell for them.

Linger on, your pale brown eyes.

poems/aadat.html.title: Aadat
poems/aadat.html.subtitle: What the heart grows used to.
poems/aadat.html.html:
I

Aaj kal unse milkar baat karke

Hume yu hi dil behelane ki aadat hai.

◆
II

Hawaon mein leherate hue bahaar ko

Humse guftugu karne ki aadat hai.

◆
III

Baarish ka mausam aaye to kher

Hume chhata bhoolne ki aadat hai.

◆
IV

Patjhad ke mausam ki tanhai ko

Humse shayari likhwane ki aadat hai.

◆
V

Afsaano mein unse door hokar

Hume purane khayalon ko anjaam dene ki aadat hai.

◆
VI

Ab majboori mein unhe bina mude

Humse door jaate dekhne ki bhi aadat hai.

poems/aangan-ke-phool.html.title: Aangan Ke Phool
poems/aangan-ke-phool.html.subtitle: When the courtyard starts to bloom again.
poems/aangan-ke-phool.html.html:
I

Aangan ke taraf aankh bhatakti reheti hai

Lagta hai ek yaad si aakar bethi hai.

◆
II

Patjhad ke girte patte udaas lagte hai

Jaane girne se pehele hi baat keh dete hai.

◆
III

Tanhai ke ghadi mein kisi ka saath nahi

Jinn phoolon ko itna sajaya wo bhi murjhaye hai.

◆
IV

Paani chaaro taraf daalne ke baad bhi

Bageeche mein ek hi phool dikhai deta hai.

◆
V

Naye phoolon ke beej lag jaye bhi to

Vo puraane phoolon ki yaad hi karaate hai.

◆
VI

Roz aziyat mein doobe raston pe bhatakte hai

Ab patjhad se kitni hi ummeed kar sakte hai.

◆
VII

Himmat nahi haari hai naye dinon ki khalvat mein

Bahaar ke phool kabhi to baraste hai.

◆
VIII

Phir bhatakti hai meri aankhe aangan mein

Lagta hai koi naya aane ko hai.

poems/after-many-seasons.html.title: After Many Seasons
poems/after-many-seasons.html.subtitle: Reunion and acceptance
poems/after-many-seasons.html.html:
I

I woke up remembering her face

A face that beamed with elegance

While life goes on without a trace

My soul now, awaits her embrace.

◆
II

I caught a glimpse of her strolling on a winter day

The cold flowers received her hand's warmth

A string of words caught at my diary's bay

Hopeless words that are filled with thorns.

◆
III

But an old regret came in like it was there

Waiting by the shore of my mind

A ghost that lingered in the salt air

Reminding me that life isn't always kind.

◆
IV

She sauntered across the garden's bridge

As if elegance was personified by her,

All I can do is pray that I get a chance

To tell her what I couldn't since that cold December.

◆
V

Her shadow falls on the fallen leaves

And as she passes by the dull daffodil

The feelingless garden now grieves

While I fail to conjure any syllable.

◆
VI

Our eyes met again on this fateful day

My heart stopped as she turned towards me

Her smile is as beautiful as the night we met in a cafe

While I just stood there thinking it wasn't to be.

◆
VII

After many seasons my umbrella found a companion,

Prattling about the good ol' days

We strolled through the sanctuary

And I pondered if eternity could feel this way.

◆
VIII

When we strolled at the end of the place

She bid me farewell at the bus stop in the rain

Leaving me alone in the garden of words

Making me hope that one day we could meet again.

◆
IX

She was a woman I once knew

Like a jasmine she poises elegantly

Even when it rains on days that are blue

While I try to move on through the lines of my poetry.

poems/almeres-fair.html.title: Almere's Fair
poems/almeres-fair.html.subtitle: A bookstore by a lake — and loves that pass through, season after season.
poems/almeres-fair.html.html:
I

Are you going to the Almere's fair?

Where the wind blows beside a field

With junipers, that rest by my lair,

As I write a poem of sorrow that I yield.

◆
II

I open my bookstore every season

Here in this crowded fair by a lake

Where travellers without any reason

Stumble upon books they forsake.

◆
III

I reminisce the day I failed

To express love in my poem,

A love which wasn't conveyed

In words, that weren't in tandem.

◆
IV

My heart remains heavy

With regret, sorrow and grief

As I walk by this field of Daisy

And Alpine that shower relief.

◆

Will you be there, my first love?

◆
V

Eating candy near a willow tree

Just like when we were thirteen,

Smiling with innocence and glee

As I stood there, with a hot caffeine.

◆

Will you pass by too, my second love?

◆
VI

Strolling by the lake in a blue dress,

In which I saw you for the first time

When my mind was in distress,

As my heart had felt pain on its dime.

◆

Will you saunter through the fair, my nostalgic love?

◆
VII

Would I find those eyes again

That I seemed to have forgotten,

While my heart braces for pain,

As it doubts the flowers that had fallen.

◆
VIII

Even in this fair's crowd, my alone

Eyes search for your long hair

And your eyes, as your cologne

Still lingers in the Spring's air.

◆

Will a new love pass through my bookstore?

◆
IX

Would my heart be paranoid

To be vulnerable over a love

That may find its place in a void

Inside my heart, that awaits a dove.

◆
X

Upon meeting her would I ever

Write again, as only the sorrow

In my lonely heart helps me lever

My hands to write for a tomorrow.

◆
XI

Will her eyes tell me a story

That is unique, making my heart

Light yet undoubtedly heavy

Unless this rigid fate plays its part.

◆
XII

Its a new season again under

This old willow tree's shade,

And it rains outside while I cover,

The books that just are a facade,

◆
XIII

For the flowers that often bloom

Just to dare the omni season,

Which is love, that brings doom

To the lover's heart, as a treason.

◆
XIV

So are you going to the Almere's fair?

poems/almost-blue.html.title: Almost Blue
poems/almost-blue.html.subtitle: A saxophone's confession.
poems/almost-blue.html.html:
I

I am almost blue

and maybe just because of you

why does it feel to be true

that I won't ever find someone like you.

◆
II

A mind as empty as mine

feels a remorse that none can subside

I think if I move towards her side

I may fall in love in a slippery slide.

◆
III

Somedays I think she is not for me

I fear to be vulnerable as a bee

as I worry to be her eyes's abductee

and I wonder if her treacherous smile could lead me somewhere,

a place where my heart feels free.

◆
IV

Yet that seems unlikely

as my saxophone blares a melody

that resonates my broken heart's fallacy

someone new has bewitched me and flew

she is a woman that could fill this heart with something new

thus my heart is almost blue

and it could be only because of you

poems/anjaan-sheher.html.title: Anjaan Sheher
poems/anjaan-sheher.html.subtitle: Life in an unknown city.
poems/anjaan-sheher.html.html:
I

Jaane kesi bandagi hai mujhe dastaan

Ek pal ki khushi ne umr bhar ke ghaav diye.

◆
II

Jis se bedilli karne ki koshish ki

Usne dua mein mujhe khoye hue armaan diye.

◆
III

Kya hi bataye haal puchne walon ko

Roz baagh mein gulab ki pankhudi tod diye.

◆
IV

Ab kaise gair ko apne jazbaat ada kare

Uss din ek baar batake gunnah to kar diye.

◆
V

Teri galiyon mein hoke hum badnaam

Kitne shehron mein apne nek naam kar diye.

◆
VI

Wo jo taameer hone wali thi bahaaron mein

Wo imarat ab barsaat mein khaali kar diye.

◆
VII

Ye dil ishq ke intezaar mein khala raha

So guftugu ki talaash mein dil fir khalvat kar diye.

◆
VIII

Zindagi iss anjaan sheher mein ab kese basar hogi

Hum to hurbat ke bagair hosh kho diye.

◆
IX

Nahi hai ab kisi aur ke liye soz-e-intezaar

Chhoti si zindagi ab tanhai mein guzaar diye.

poems/at-the-turn-of-a-hill.html.title: At the Turn of a Hill
poems/at-the-turn-of-a-hill.html.subtitle: A chance encounter
poems/at-the-turn-of-a-hill.html.html:
I

The flower shop at the turn of a hill

Keeps all the pretty flowers at one place

While the cold wind in a shrill

Flips the pages of my book that is with me for grace

◆
II

Her hair flows like the sea

Displaying each curve of her wavy form

I wonder if it really is autumn by this tree

As her presence seems like a spring's affair

◆
III

The clouds that were darkening over me

Were banished by the winds of her stride

I was mesmerised by her eyes that fled

From mine that looked at her with delight

◆
IV

Flowers of jasmine danced at the tune of her emotions

I could notice she had an epiphany

As her hands were flipping a book's pages

And I couldn't help but smile at her symphony

◆
V

A hint of blush on her cheeks

As our eyes meet at the romance shelf

I pick a novel which reminisces a past love

Wondering if there is a future on this hill as I dwell

◆
VI

On the hope that shall rescue me from this shrill

Hinting me towards a new beginning

Guiding me through the end of this misery

I was reborn when I saw her at the turn of a hill

◆
VII

It was enough for me to concede

And saunter ahead with a blank slate

While I share this coffee with her that is sweet

Making me hopeful for a turn of fate.

poems/before-we-grey.html.title: Before We Grey
poems/before-we-grey.html.subtitle: Four years. Before our hair turns grey.
poems/before-we-grey.html.html:
I

At a distance, autumn is green

But my heart keeps feeling blue.

Although life spent here was routine

Yet these memories always seem new.

◆
II

Now its the twilight days of school

The memories seem surreal

All the friends made are still cool

And these four years, we did only dream.

◆
III

Maybe we meet again in an autumn

When our hair may have turned grey,

And as we tell our stories with optimism

I hope these memories don't fade away.

poems/bekashi-ka-saya.html.title: Bekashi Ka Saya
poems/bekashi-ka-saya.html.subtitle: The shadow that homesickness casts.
poems/bekashi-ka-saya.html.html:
I

Aaj kal sheher mein apne gaon ki yaad mein khoya sa rehta hoon

Lagta hai mere panno ko teri ada-e-bekashi phir chha gayi.

◆
II

Maine ek umr se apni kitaab mein sambhali hui hai

Wahi tasveer jo ek pal bhi nahi dekhi gayi.

◆
III

Gulshan murjha raha hai teri haseen ghataon ke bagair

So ab bhi mere dil mein teri yaadein kyo nahi murjha gayi.

◆
IV

Mere naseeb mein ek phool khilne ko laga sada ki mehrumi

Par aakhir mein na itminan hua na hi tujhe pyaar.

◆
V

Main jaan-e-bahaara tujhe bhulake khush hona chahta hoon

Par ye kambaqt yadaash dil ke liye khanjar bankar reh gayi.

◆
VI

Mujhe koi acha bhi nahi lagta humnaam tera

Ab koi tujsa nahi mila tha to pyaar se ummed chali gayi.

◆
VII

Par inn dino phir mausam beimaan sa lagne laga hai

Aisa afasana hai ke panno mein kisi naye ki ada-e-aafat si chha gayi.

poems/cafe-in-march.html.title: The Café in March
poems/cafe-in-march.html.subtitle: What a café window reveals.
poems/cafe-in-march.html.html:
I

I cross puddles formed by

the drizzle of rain in March

which I often foolishly pry

on this lane and in my scotch.

◆
II

I hear the faint chirping

of birds while I saunter

by a garden, pondering

about feelings that linger.

◆
III

Peculiar thoughts chased

my mind while I sipped coffee

in a café as I remained dazed

by a woman who chose to flee,

 

from my heart and my poem

that remains wry and incomplete

to this day as my pen in tandem

has yet to live up to its conceit.

◆
IV

I see the world ever changing

while I stay in this café's shade

taking my time and observing

how with life, my emotions fade.

◆
V

I notice a mother without a ring

who has two kids by her side,

frantic to share her loneliness

but is clueless where to confide.

◆
VI

I spotted an old man drown

in his sorrows and in his drink

while his shirt that was brown

had seen grief without a blink.

◆
VII

I caught a glimpse of a woman

who has eyes that were blue

drank a juice that had lemon

and had an umbrella that was blue.

◆
VIII

My teary eyes await the rain

as only my rhymes get to know

and see me cry in the nights of pain

while life just seems to flow.

 

Rain in the midst of March, made

me see a scene that has shades

and are now etched under this shade

as I write about how it all fades.

poems/dariya.html.title: Dariya
poems/dariya.html.subtitle: The River. A strange affliction called love.
poems/dariya.html.html:
Ye dillagi bhi kaisi anokhi bimari hai

Itne din beet gaye tab bhi yaad suhani hai.

Tez hawa ne mujhse pucha

Iss mohabbat se sawaal puche sabne hai.

Humse na pucho ye beete hijr ke kisse

Har kisse mein unki beparwahi ka zikr hai.

Ye cigarette ka dhua le aata hai saath samundar paar

Hume kya pata tha ye yaadein bhi beheti hai.

Ab kis khushakismat ko tum chaahton se dekhte ho

Barbaadi dekh kar bhi hum haat malte hai.

Hum ghazal mein tumhara naam nahi zikr hone dete

Inn yaad bhare khaton ko rusvan nahi hone dete hai.

Ye jaam roz rooh ko pyasi kar deti hai

Pyaas hi sahi phir ye udaasi kahan se dhundh laati hai.

poems/does-the-rain-ever-fall.html.title: Does the Rain Ever Fall on Us
poems/does-the-rain-ever-fall.html.subtitle: A conversation under the rain.
poems/does-the-rain-ever-fall.html.html:
I

Does the rain ever fall on us as a sign?

She asked me in an apologetic tone

I wondered if it was raining in her heart or mine

while I stood beside her, blessed by her cologne.

◆
II

Does the windy rain make you shiver?

I asked her while the breezy wind blew

her hair that personified peace like a river

while I fell in love with eyes that were blue.

◆
III

Does the rain ever fail to embrace?

She asked me so nonchalantly

while I looked at her with a lonely face

and answered the question honestly.

◆
IV

Rain is my close friend indeed

it helps me hide my sorrowful tears

and helps me smile without any greed

that I had hid in my heart for years.

◆
V

I also often seek the early morning rain

and its haunting yet merciful pain

while I wondered if my heart could ever feign

for a grieving tomorrow, that follows me in the rain.

◆
VI

While the raindrops fell on her heavenly skin

I thanked God for this gracious day of July

while my fountain pen and I, live a life of sin,

as I wrote a small poem on a butterfly.

◆
VII

A silence engulfed in the air, and I dreaded

a haunting verse that came into my head

and as rain fell on this crooked shade

I wondered if I was actually living or dead.

◆
VIII

Did the rain take us on a journey yet?

I thought out loud as my love for her

spoke in silence and her hair that was wet

felt like a sight that could make me quiver.

◆
IX

When the rain untimely stopped

we stepped outside, from the shade

and the garden that was swamped

while I wished that we had stayed.

◆
X

Will we ever happen to meet on this long road?

I thought to myself as we bid adieu in charade

we went our separate ways, and as I started for my abode

I looked back and noticed a smile on her face.

◆
XI

A smile so hauntingly beautiful in that outwind

made my heart long for her and almost made me pursue

those feelings for her, that have now withered in the wind

leaving only memories, that I also meant to bid adieu.

◆
XII

Does the rainy sky ever fill you with hope?

I wondered as several seasons had went by

I prayed, that I could meet her once more on this life's slope

and to be in love with a girl that could make me sway.

◆
XIII

As I walk along this nostalgic garden

that had once helped me write a poem

now only flowers blossom here that seem golden

as the blue sky filled the scenery in tandem.

◆
XIV

I stroll under this blue and rainy sky

endless thoughts cross my poetic mind

I recall the memory of a girl from a July

while rain falls on me and my timid hind

 

I wished once more, under this shade

to meet her again in this rainy place

now I pray one more time, as I delayed

the thoughts that longingly chase,

 

for a simple twist of fate.

poems/door-jaake-basi.html.title: Door Jaake Basi
poems/door-jaake-basi.html.subtitle: A ghazal of longing across distance
poems/door-jaake-basi.html.html:
I

Tu jab door jaake basi to mere qareeb lagi

Khuda hi jaane ye dil ab kya mod lega.

◆
II

Rubaru meri dhadkan bhi samajhne lagi

Ke tujhse milane ko sama ab kayi muddat lega.

◆
III

Ek hi jijhak raha haal-e-dil sudhaarne mein

Ke ye fasaana fir kahi tera zikr lega.

◆
IV

Jo apne dil pe guzari hai wo koi kya jaane

Isi umeed mein jeele ke dil tujhe bhula lega.

◆
V

Ab kese kisi se marasim badhaye hum

Yahi dar hai ke koi marasim tujh tak pahuncha lega.

◆
VI

Fir koi nayi pur-kashish qareeb aa rahi hai

Iski ada gulshan se jaane mein waqt lega.

◆
VII

Dil-e-nadaan iss halchal ka pata bata

Jo ishq dekar mera dard lega.

◆
VIII

Bahaar kata rahe hain chalte chalte

Afsos ye gulshan meri yaadein lega.

◆
IX

Sahulat se guzar jao meri jaan

Ye mohabbat sach mein meri jaan lega.

poems/dusky-window.html.title: Dusky Window
poems/dusky-window.html.subtitle: Time passed — transparent as the gushing wind, hollow in its wake.
poems/dusky-window.html.html:
I

The time that passed is like a dusky window

It seemed transparent like the gushing wind

But what has passed remains hollow

From the emotions that seldom rescind.

◆
II

You can see through the memory

But it's the emotion that brings storms

And as it all becomes a melancholy

The reminiscence slowly deforms.

◆
III

Conversing about time that has passed

Is an activity for people who are strife

Who find time that has amassed

In this maze seldom called life.

◆
IV

As the cigarette leaves my lips

I ponder if memories are canned by fate

In the store of my subconscious which slips

When it returns memories with an expiry date.

◆
V

I exhale the smoke while reminiscing a time

When she strolled beside me in October

Her again on these nostalgic crossroads.

◆

As most of them should be

And when this soul does perish

I'll choose to vanish with this memory.

poems/eleventh-of-april.html.title: 11th of April
poems/eleventh-of-april.html.subtitle: A date that stays in the blood.
poems/eleventh-of-april.html.html:
I

I saunter among the autumn

leaves that have turned brown

while I write a melancholic poem

about my life, as I foolishly drown.

◆
II

I drown in these nonsensical

emotions that do overwhelm

me, and my pen which remain fatal

on this rainy day, that I condemn.

◆
III

I take refuge under a lonely shade

and I ponder about the signal

that my heart has for the dead

feelings that forcefully linger.

◆
IV

I place my hands onto the wood

that has become fragile with time

I realised that I never understood

how a caterpillar could climb.

◆
V

I see raindrops falling on a flower

that seeps through the shade

leaving no space for any answer

about life, that I wanted in charade.

◆
VI

While I was searching for clarity

I stumbled on this rainy and peaceful

place that makes me forget reality

but I only write a rhyme too painful.

◆
VII

11th of April, I had gotten a message

from her that was hurting in tandem

with the thoughts that lay vestige

in my mind and in my sorrowful poem.

◆
VIII

Now it's a rainy day of August

a month that only makes promises

of cold and chilly winds with trust

but now it rains on flowers of hibiscus.

 

I hear the ticking of my watch

that is damp from the frisky rain

and I crave for a rocks on scotch

so that I could feel like a swain.

 

I finish this poem that was due

and I walk past a moist flower

with an umbrella that is blue

which she gave me on a September.

 

I put the poem inside the bag

and I open the rusty parasol

to protect the bag from the rain

as it has a poem and a photograph.

 

It's a poem about her

and a photograph of us.

poems/empty-reasons.html.title: Empty Reasons
poems/empty-reasons.html.subtitle: A poem of loss, written on the spot
poems/empty-reasons.html.html:
I

Hefty winds blow by my abode

Bringing the desolating weather

That changes direction of a door

That brings me another trice without her.

◆
II

Another spring without her mention

As I walk into my garden that does wither

I reminisce in those warm memories of affection

That has left this fallow garden, along with her.

◆
III

Another summer approaches, where her eyes

Do not throw shade on my heart that is frail,

Making me wish that this poem flies

To a place where her conscience gets to bail.

◆
IV

Another rain without the sight of the blue umbrella

That protected her from rain as she sauntered

Past the gallery, elegantly into a cappella

At the theatre without any nerves watered.

◆
V

This is to her and always her

I am pleased to where to she is heading

I wish her the best for the upcoming future,

As I continue to never cross paths with her.

◆
VI

As another spring ends without her mention,

I write to commit a poetic treason

As she still carelessly without contention

Cuts through my frail heart and its reason.

poems/eyes-almost-blue.html.title: Eyes Almost Blue
poems/eyes-almost-blue.html.subtitle: She carried your eyes in a different face.
poems/eyes-almost-blue.html.html:
I

One rainy evening,

I heard an old tune from a street

I stood under a shade as heavy rain came down in a heartbeat

I lit a cigarette for my pain that almost made my heart weep.

◆
II

This rain brings memories wrapped in tears

I realised that the poems I write have always been about you,

a woman of my past, a memory that nobody shares.

◆
III

My eyes closed as I listened to that melody

a melody that had reminisces of your melancholy

memories that linger in this symphony

and cling onto a breeze that resembles my heart's fallacy.

◆
IV

A vendor smiles and sways to this melody's magic

a simple twist of fate had made its tactic

as I caught a glimpse of a woman who could prove that love is in itself, tragic

the rain was spinning a story that had no logic

I realised I may fall in love with her and felt pathetic.

◆
V

I caught a glimpse of her eyes that were almost blue

my heartbeat stopped for that moment when she looked into my eyes too

I became eager to write about her and this scenery as it all felt too good to be true.

◆
VI

My heart felt light yet heavy

I had forgotten this feeling that has retraced back to me as my heart felt a bit rainy

I see her drying her wet hair under the same shade, while she wore a smile that could wound any man that seemed dreamy

we both looked at the street that has a past memory.

◆
VII

This woman who stands five feet beside me carries a peculiar reminiscent of you

I know that to be absurd yet my heart feels it to be true

her blue eyes look my way and I fear it might only be you

my eyes look into hers that moment and just as a car passed by us, my eyes flew.

◆
VIII

For the first time, I didn't despise the rain

in the past it only showed my unbearable pain

fate always felt cruel, twisting my life as it only made tragedy remain

but now I stand beside a woman that makes me want to fall in love again.

◆
IX

I saw people write about love but I thought it was not meant for me

all I have managed to write about is heartbreak as my heart is yet to be free

now as I talk with this woman, I hope to make my heart a guarantee

a guarantee of a love that could remain within me and without me.

◆
X

We both smiled with glee

we looked at the rain drenched streets where people just flee

the rain was heavy and our umbrella was as useless as a bee

I started falling in love with her and with this place that had made me its abductee.

◆
XI

We waited for the rain to become calmer

yet I prayed for the rain to be harsher

 

And again we stood waiting

for a memory that was yet to be reaching

then the melody made me start humming

a tune that prompted me of you and your eyes that were always shining

I realised that I hadn't forgotten about you although I shouldn't be longing.

◆
XII

I stood there, calming my heart

I braced myself for another wound

as I had decided to find a love for this woman that has made my heart fall apart

 

She is reading an anthology while sharing glances with me in silence

my heart beats as fast as I can imagine and runs out of patience

as I look at the rain, I call out a poem from the book she was reading in solace.

 

"A faint clap of thunder clouded skies perhaps rain comes again if so, stay with me?"

 

She smiles in a calm manner and replies

 

"A faint clap of thunder even if rain comes not I will stay here together with you and if it rains, I wonder if you would stay here too?"

 

My mind went blank in joy, then I perceived a reply that I had given to you several seasons ago, to this same verse.

But I couldn't say it out loud as it seemed like a curse.

Yet I said it in my mind, as it wasn't something I could just subside.

"Even if it doesn't rain, I'll be here, waiting for you or someone like you."

 

I stood there, feeling guilty of falling for someone other than you

yet she feels almost you

I saw your eyes in her that are almost blue

yet I still wait for a simple twist of fate that could for once, make it all true.

A distant rumble of thunder,

clouded skies.

Perhaps rain comes again —

if so, will you stay with me?

I will stay here with you —

and if it rains, would you stay too?

The poet, to no one in particular

Even if it doesn't rain,

I'll be here,

waiting for you,

or someone like you.

poems/gazing-at-flowers.html.title: Gazing at Flowers
poems/gazing-at-flowers.html.subtitle: Life goes on within you and without you.
poems/gazing-at-flowers.html.html:
We were gazing at the flowers as we wryly smiled through the darkness in our hearts, searching desperately for the light that could guide us through our paths.

Birds fly away from the melancholy of my life as I hide my grief and the tears behind this mask I wear on my face.

The peaceful birds which had become accustomed to the silence inside of me, now are desperate to rejoice in the thrill which I have long lost.

The pain in my heart which was like a nonchalant voice, now becomes a solace for this old soul's void.

Everything which was of importance in my life, now feels mundane as I plunge out of the depths of my longing sorrows, yet I fall shortly after, into another depthless void of grief and bittersweet hollows.

I often feel as if we all are travellers, looking for a purpose or solitude amidst the inclemencies in our life's purposes. The love that we all possess, guide us through this vast ocean of emotions, acting like a passage, steering us through our agitations.

This solitude which we seek, is rather diminishing as we hide the emotions which make us look weak. With time, we come to terms with the magic we all have. All the love, peace and calm that we seek is already in us, we don't need to search for it as the great passage of words and emotions guide us to our own heart and we realise that, life goes on within you and without you.

poems/ghaav-ki-khushboo.html.title: Ghaav Ki Khushboo
poems/ghaav-ki-khushboo.html.subtitle: Even wounds carry a fragrance.
poems/ghaav-ki-khushboo.html.html:
I

Jab tere yaad ke ghaav bharne lagte hai

Ek yaad ki khushboo fir mehsoos karne hoon.

◆
II

Baagh mein jab gulab ko titaliyan satati hai

Tab bahaane mein tumhe yaad karne lagta hoon.

◆
III

Kesa sannata chhaya hai iss ghar mein ya Rab

Har shaam sirf pal-e-tanhai ka hi tajurba kare ja raha hoon.

◆
IV

Kitabon ke beech jab jab apne ko khone laga

Tab tab zehen se fisli tazkaron ko inn panno mein pata hoon.

◆
V

Kyon sukoon ke pal ab sabab mangte hai

Aisi madhoshi hai ke nazm ab sukoon ke liye likhta hoon.

◆
VI

Ab kon hi fark kare sukh ya dukh mein

Madari reheke lamho mein bikhar gaya hoon.

◆
VII

Ab baagh mein phul to saare jhad gaye

Chalo, murjhaye phulon se pehechan phir kar leta hoon.

◆
VIII

Phool wapis khilne ka anjaam kabhi to denge iss baagh ko

Main to bas anjaam ke intezaar mein lamhe kata raha hoon.

poems/girl-with-cat-named-whiskey.html.title: The Girl with a Cat Named Whiskey
poems/girl-with-cat-named-whiskey.html.subtitle: Sugarless coffee and fading warmth
poems/girl-with-cat-named-whiskey.html.html:
I

This cold evening makes me reminisce

A time with her cat and her wry smile

Filling my hands with warmth and bliss

And memories of old now fade.

◆
II

My book of poetry drenched in blue

Remains a melancholy that hinders

My wait for a love that has been due

For countless lonely winters.

◆
III

On a cold December night she had caught my attention

When flowers were nowhere to be seen

Now a spring arrives without her mention

And flowers in the garden seem routine.

◆
IV

The cat drew me towards her in mystery

I was not fond of cats which were furry

And especially not one named whiskey

But the heart yearned change in a hurry.

◆
V

I recall sitting in her patio listening to her with sugarless coffee

Prattling about life while whiskey would sit on my jacket

Listening to our conversations as a hobby

And we would kiss, which had become a habit.

◆
VI

Nowadays I make my coffee with less sugar

I drink it with a cigarette in my hand

While I try to put a name on this feeling

That blew away with the wind as planned.

poems/hairpin.html.title: The Hairpin
poems/hairpin.html.subtitle: Written for the ones who go to war
poems/hairpin.html.html:
I

It's a lonely Saturday, I watch the jet planes fly into oblivion

Lying on my roof, I spectate as a memory burns away

With the cigarette, that burned beside me wailing as it lay.

◆
II

First view of the city is always different in the morning

I see it, the boy cries a little less as he gets flimsy

And the windows, of the old building seem a little less dusty.

◆
III

Shelter from the storm, I was given when I passed her way

It was another lifetime, when everything was new and bold

A transient memory, which is now old.

◆
IV

Not a word was spoken, the first time I met her gaze

The rain showered, heavily upon us on this old alleyway

I could hear piano strings, in my heart playing away.

◆
V

I hoped, that I won't fall in love with her

Since love, never fails to make me blue

And as the whistle blows, I boarded the train that was always due.

◆
VI

I bid her farewell, and as a tear fell from her cheek

The train started, moving in a motion swift

While I did not confess, these feelings that I had wrapped in a gift.

◆
VII

It was a hairpin, that she once was mesmerised by

Now it remains, with me forever hidden

As I had gone to war, for people to be ridden.

◆
VIII

When I came back, with an artificial eye

Which only sees the past, a time with her

And the other, sees a hairpin and jet planes since December.

poems/hawa-ke-dastaan.html.subtitle: Stories the wind carries home.
poems/hawa-ke-dastaan.html.html:
Ae pichle mausam ke saathi

Ab ke baras aas paas bas tanhai hai.

Likhta hoon ghazal auron ke liye

Mere wo ghazal bhi tumhare naam hai.

Yun to apne nazuk se dil ke paas

Jaane kis kiske paighaam hai.

Koi puche to main kya bataun

Mere har khat tumhare naam hai.

Thak gaya hun mein iss bhag daud se

poems/homeward-bound.html.title: Homeward Bound
poems/homeward-bound.html.subtitle: Going back to a city that no one calls home.
poems/homeward-bound.html.html:
I

This car won't slow down in dim light

Even with the heavy riverside wind

Pushing against it with a might

Which makes it seem like a headwind.

◆
II

The winds blow here ferociously

Along these country roads with a sunshine

That caresses my heavy heart tenderly

Beside these fields of Juniper & Alpine.

◆
III

A nostalgic memory races my mind's lair

As the highway wind hits my face

And brushes through my messy hair

While sun shines brightly on my charade.

◆
IV

I recall the times when fruits were collected

From the lakeside farms that were near

Our place where everyone gathered

And came to the country home I hold dear.

◆
V

Grandparents, uncles, aunts, cousins,

Every one of them visited to enjoy

The cool summer breeze, that now

Blows with an empty ahoy

As time slipped through & didn't allow,

◆
VI

Me to even bid farewell to the people

I held in great regard and affection,

Now I stand in these fields that has a beetle

Climbing on a branch with no conviction.

◆
VII

The beetle reminded me of myself

A kid who's ignorance was bliss

Now I see is a world that has scared itself

From words that feign love in distress.

◆
VIII

Confabulating with the people around

I spent my summer days there in solace

Now I am bound to my city with a frown

On my face & with boots without shoelace.

◆
IX

The old people that once had stayed

Already died in a simple twist of fate.

So I had visited today, that tragic shade

To pay respects in silence while I did wait.

◆
X

With feelings overwhelming to the core

I write this poem as I travel to the airport

With stuff that I bought from the store

Where people smiled to heal scars in rapport.

◆
XI

I wish to be homeward bound in reality

Except, I am going to a place

That I can hardly call a home in fidelity

So I write this verse with a mask on my face.

◆
XII

The place I go back to with a frown

Has no one to even call my own

Hypocrites, surround me as I drown

In the sea of words that I have never known.

◆
XIII

No lover waits for me back in the city

The one whom I loved long ago had left

And now this place that I leave is empty

Except for a blue bird that lies with its nest.

◆
XIV

Never could I see the stars in the city

Yet to write beneath the diamond sky

In that country town in tranquility

Is how I would like my nights to go by.

◆
XV

The town has flowers glittered

That never bend in the rainfall

But now the flowers in the city have withered

As there hasn't been sunshine since fall.

◆
XVI

All these places have their own memories

Well it be the city or that town since years,

Yet I enjoyed my days in the windy breeze

Of my childhood place that I leave in tears.

◆
XVII

Though I know I will never lose a love innate

For people and things that went before

But I know that they will stay in my shade

As they are in my poems that I still explore.

◆
XVIII

These memories will stay in this poem

And I will continue to pretend that

These memories will remain in tandem

As I know I'll often think about those,

 

Flowers that never bend with the rainfall,

 

And the wind that blows through the countryside.

poems/hum-kahan-jayenge.html.title: Hum Kahan Jayenge
poems/hum-kahan-jayenge.html.subtitle: A ghazal of parting
poems/hum-kahan-jayenge.html.html:
I

Hai qayanaat-e-mehfil saji humare liye

Tum kaha jaoge, hum kaha jayenge.

◆
II

Logon ki to aadat hai bichhadna

Lapata sab hai par, hum kaha jayenge.

◆
III

Raatein kat ti nahi ab pehele jaisi

Tere khyaal mein doob kar, hum kaha jayenge.

◆
IV

Ab wo peheli si guftugu nahi tumhare saath

Unn palon ko yaad karke, hum kaha jayenge.

◆
V

Koi hasil na tha aarzu ka magar

Be-aarzu tumse alag hogaye, hum kaha jayenge.

◆
VI

Kabhi kabhi yun lagta hai ke tum laut aayega

Par ab mile bhi to hum kaha jaayenge.

◆
VII

Dil se dil milana chahta hoon firse lekin

Dil-o-jaan to tumne rakh liya, hum kaha jayenge.

◆
VIII

Ek hi baat hai jo ek baras se kehena chaaha

Dil ki baat kehekar bhi, hum kaha jayenge.

◆
IX

Tum kyon phirse inhi raston mein mujhe chhod aaye

Ab yahaan se wapis hum kaha jayenge.

◆
X

Ab bikharne ko hai ye teri meri daastaan-e-rang-o-bu

Tum kaha jaaoge hum kaha jayenge.

poems/in-the-rain.html.title: In the Rain
poems/in-the-rain.html.subtitle: For a friend lost to the rain.
poems/in-the-rain.html.html:
I

This rain that pours me with sorrow and grief

also took away my world's only relief.

My friend, who smiled brightly even when the nights felt shallow,

left his loved ones and this world which had made him hollow.

So many days have slipped by

but this agony doesn't pass by.

This distress often returns in my life,

like the rain which doesn't know when to confide.

◆
II

In just two years, we had found a brother in each other,

but we never found closure for the crosses we had borne for the other.

While I never realised how greatly I would regret

for not helping you when you were in need,

I went on with my life with this anguish in my heart which never deceased.

I walk with regret on this life's slope,

and I stroll on this lonely road which has fell silent

without your voice filled with hope.

They remind me of all those memories that now seem bittersweet,

of us having a laugh about how life had its fair share of sour and sweet.

◆
III

Now as I move on with my life, I carry a sheet filled with poems,

about a friend whom I lost amidst the rain filled with regrets and sorrows.

So as I move on in life and write these poems

under the roof of an old soul who looks to pay his amend,

thus I could only hope

that you would think about me every now and then,

old friend.

poems/intezaar.html.title: Intezaar
poems/intezaar.html.subtitle: The only thing that stays.
poems/intezaar.html.html:
Dil mein ab soz-e-intezaar to raha nahi

Tumne ye hi baat meri maan li thi kya.

Bheegi raatein meri aankhon ki nami chhipa rahi hai

Ab aankhon mein tujhe mehfooz rakhna bhi gunnah hai kya.

Mere sab ishq-e-alfaaz beasar hi rahe

Main koi alag desh jaa chuka hoon kya.

Itne haseen chehre hai to mere ird gird

Par tum jaisa koi milna mumkin bhi hai kya.

Ye patjhad bhi mujhe chain kyon nahi de raha

Ek hi shaks tha jahaan mein kya.

Ye pal hai jo guzara nahi jaa raha humse

Ab humne wo zindagi nahi guzari kya.

Kalam to maujud rahega jab koi naya bhi aaye

Par tum jaisi koi alqa iss aalam mein hai kya.

Naye kaliyon se fir mulaqat karne nikle ke kahi tera roop dikh jaye

Par aise haalat bhi humse jaan pehechan rakhte hai kya.

poems/it-not-as-if.html.title: It's Not As If
poems/it-not-as-if.html.subtitle: The confession hidden in denial
poems/it-not-as-if.html.html:
I

It's not as if I wandered my office to get a glimpse of you,

Walking the hallway while nervously fixing my watch.

It's not as if I anxiously waited to talk to you,

Plotting ways to somehow see you again.

◆
II

It's not as if I saw you in the books I read,

Or in the garden with the pretty sunflowers that resemble your smile.

It's not as if I bought you that gift you liked,

After consulting everyone who knew me.

◆
III

It's not as if something burned inside me,

When I saw you leaving the town.

It's not as if I lie to everyone,

When I say that I don't dream about you anymore.

◆
IV

It's not as if you've made yourself a home in my heart,

Or in my poem that mentions your blessed eyes.

I can't help but admit that this ballad is real,

As real as my heart that beats faster at your mention.

◆
V

Now an autumn reaches my doorstep

As my heart shifts from blue to autumn's orange

I remain hopeful for the next day.

poems/ive-known-life.html.title: I've Known Life
poems/ive-known-life.html.subtitle: I've known only one thing that flows through everything.
poems/ive-known-life.html.html:
I

My blurred and teary sight

Watches the leaves of a tree

Dance to the tunes of the rain

While I write a poem about a bee.

◆
II

I watch as the rain drops pour

On my desolated shade,

I reminisce a time that bore

Sorrows in my life's charade.

◆
III

As the lush green leaves fall

Reminding me the fall of twenty

When a love stayed unrequited

From a joyful & hopeful reality.

◆
IV

These chilly and cold winds

Write a melancholic story

About the grieve stricken fields

In the broken hearted diary.

◆
V

My watch is soaked in the rain

And raindrops fall & slide down

The watch while I smoke in vain

Wishing if that could ever change.

◆
VI

My rusty bicycle is just for show

It reminds me of my childhood

When life was just too slow

And time was spent for good.

◆
VII

Cold winds accompany the rains

While people just don't mind

How the lonely world feigns

A joy which is only found inside.

◆
VIII

A sorrowful night is received

As the day ends and the rain

Is visible only under the street

Lights that show a way again.

◆
IX

Now as the lonesome hours

And chilly minutes pass by,

I have known only one thing

That flows through everything,

◆
X

I've known life.

poems/jaan-e-baharan.html.title: Jaan-e-Baharan
poems/jaan-e-baharan.html.subtitle: The spring that was.
poems/jaan-e-baharan.html.html:
I

Ek jaan-e-baharaan jaan humari thi

Kayi mausam pehlee ki baat thi, ab to koi baat hi nahi.

◆
II

Wo jo hava ke jhaunke si guzar gayi

Unko to humari ab koi bhi khabar nahi.

◆
III

Uske khayalon ke bina koi aur soch nahi thi

Soch to wahi rahi par wo paas nahi.

◆
IV

Har pal khilte phulon ki janib to kar mat

Haal ab unn phulon ko bhi dekh ke theek nahi.

◆
V

Aaj naye mausamo ke liye beqarar to hai

Par wo purani barsaat ke siva aangan mein kuch nahi.

◆
VI

Ab to jaan nisaar kisi aur ke liye kaha hi hoga Raahi,

Waisa sa behaal hona to kisi aur ke liye nahi.

poems/jaayega-kahan-ab.html.title: Jaayega Kahan Ab
poems/jaayega-kahan-ab.html.subtitle: A ghazal of the wanderer's question
poems/jaayega-kahan-ab.html.html:
I

Ye chand lamho ki baarish bhi ab

Kisi aur ke chhat pe baras gayi ab.

◆
II

Tumhare jaane anjaane ne kar diya bura haal

Tere mere sapne kabhi ek rang na honge ab.

◆
III

Jab dukh sukh baantne ke liye sahaara dhundhta fira

Par var diga tune bhi meri baat suni nahi ab.

◆
IV

Jiske liye sher-o-shayari se guftugu fir shuru ki thi

Wo hi mere kalam tutne ka wajah bana ab.

◆
V

Ye raat ye chandni fir kaha,

Raahi tu bhi ruton ka ghulam ban chuka hai ab.

◆
VI

Har cheez mein jo tu patjhad aur bahaar dhunde firta hai

Wahaan kon hai tera, musafir,

jayega kahan ab?

◆
VII

Waqt ko zaya kar kitne gham-e-shaam bitayega ab?

Teri manzil hai yahi, jaayega kahan ab?

poems/jessie.html.subtitle: For the syllables I couldn't think of in a poem.
poems/jessie.html.html:
I

It's been a long time since I last heard you sing. Somedays I just find myself looking at your photograph while my heart just grieves.

◆
II

Now you have grown your hair and moved somewhere, a place where I could never come close to. I arrived at that place yet I remained distanced, a shimmering thought stopped me, making me blue.

◆
III

You never owed me anything, yet I owe everything I know about love and life, to you.

◆
IV

You were the syllables I couldn't think of in a poem and you were the melody that lacked in my symphony.

◆
V

I visualise you in my poetry, dancing with words in the garden of my heart while I aimlessly await your return to these rain drenched streets that are empty.

◆
VI

In my mind, you float across my lonely and grieving waters. With just a glimpse of your smile, my mind dispels all my horrors.

◆
VII

Some seasons ago, I read you in some kind of a poem. I shivered when I wondered how poets had come across love that felt like anguish for me and for them.

◆
VIII

I played my guitar one lonely evening, it wept through a soothing melody that felt blue, a tune that reminded me of how ill fated I was for not being with you.

◆
IX

A poem over you often feels undone. Then I wonder why I spend my time, writing poems that I can't believe, writing words that resemble you yet feel ridiculous when they rhyme.

◆
X

If she could read my mind, she could see a tale unfolding itself, a tale that lets me visualise her, standing still under the moonlight in Vermont.

◆
XI

When I can not sing my heart, I can only speak my mind. Then I write on these meaningless sheets, filling my heart out and I let the words sing a melody, a melody that has faint reminisces of you.

◆
XII

I may forget to write once I get old, I may forget the lies and the truths of my present and past, but the only truth worth remembering, would be you.

◆
XIII

Half of what I said is meaningless, but I said it just to reach you. Several seasons have passed and I couldn't reach you, so I write this poem of love for you, Jessie.

poems/jhuti-tasalli.html.title: Jhuti Tasalli
poems/jhuti-tasalli.html.subtitle: The lies a poet tells himself.
poems/jhuti-tasalli.html.html:
Apne mann ki awaaz ko geet samajh, gaano mein uski yaadein dhundta fir, apne dil ki guzaarish ko suljhata firta hoon.

Apne aap ko shayar samajh, shayari suna suna kar, apne rooh ko jhuti tasalli de raha hoon.

Apne aap ko kavi samajh, uski aankhon ke saaya ko shabdo mein baya karne ki koshish hi karta reh gaya hun.

Apne aap ko aashiq samajh, kayi ankahi dastayein banane ki saazish kar betha hoon.

Iss sharab aur ye qalam se inn kagazon mein usko amar karne ka jurm apne bhooj pe lekhe bhatakte fir raha hoon.

poems/khaali-gali.html.title: Khaali Gali
poems/khaali-gali.html.subtitle: Empty lanes, empty evenings.
poems/khaali-gali.html.html:
Aaj kal mere gali se to koi nahi guzar raha

To hum gali gali se guzar rahe hai kisi ke liye.

Gul phir khilne ko bechain hai iss bahaar-e-gulshan mein

Dil-e-nadaan jald baazi mein kuch nahi hai paane ke liye.

Apni khuli zulfe lapetke bethi hai ek husn pari samne

Kaise batlaye ke ab kuch nahi iss dil mein dene ke liye.

Uske sawalon ka jawaab tha to magar diya nahi

Hass aur diye ashk aankhon ke chupane ke liye.

Lagta hai ab uske ishq mein naye tajurbe dekhne ko milenge

Par aisa to nahi ke ye raste naye mere kalaam ke liye.

Apni befikri mein guzar jao meri jaan

Humara ek din ka sath jo thehra wo kaafi hai zindagi bhar ki yaadon ke liye.

Ek aur ajnabi haseena se guftugu ki arzoo to hai

Par beqarari ae dil tujhe na hua waisa sa kisi aur ke liye.

poems/khawab-ki-dakhili.html.title: Khawab Ki Dakhili
poems/khawab-ki-dakhili.html.subtitle: When a dream walks in uninvited.
poems/khawab-ki-dakhili.html.html:
I

Kayi Raatein Guzar Gaye,

Uss bewaqt khwab ko dekhe

Hue, jisne mujhe mausamo

Mein badlav dikhana chhod diya.

◆
II

Wo Raat, ittar ki khushboo

Jaisi ladki mere khwaab

Mein ayi aur mere zaalim

Naseeb ki dastaan bangayi.

◆
III

Neele aur khule ambar

Ke neeche, aur baharon

Ki hawaon ki maujudigi

Mein, meine tumko paya.

◆
IV

Neele jharne ki tarah, tum

Bhi mere uss khwaab mein,

Neeli saari pehenke mere

Dil ki takdeere mitane ayi thi.

◆
V

Sadak pe tumhare saath

Chalte hue na waqt ka

Andaaza hua na lihaaz hua,

Bas tumhari hasi ka nasha hua.

◆
VI

Tumhare baalo ki lehero mein

Ghum hone ki saajish karte

Fir raha tha. Par tumhari aankho

Ne saajish ka mauka hi nahi diya.

◆
VII

Ye khwab tut gaya jab

Subah, baarish ki bundo

Ne mere khidki se, meri shayri

Ke panno mein dakhili paya.

◆
VIII

Ab kayi mausam beet gaye,

Ab kayi panchiyo se ishq

Karne ki koshish ki, par

Tum jaisi panchi nahi mili.

◆
IX

Na ab khwabo mein kahi

Dikhti ho na kisi kitabcha

Ke kone mein, aur na hi

Kisi akhbaar ke panno mein.

◆
X

Bas mere zindagi mein kahi

Bhi maujood ho, to meri nazm

Mein, aur mere shayrion mein

Jo ik kali ki intezaar mein hai.

◆
XI

Ab firse ye zindagi bahar

Leke aya hai, phool gulte

Hai to bas unmein tumhari

Hassi aur chhavi dikhti hai.

◆
XII

Ab mein iss patjhad ke mausam

Mein, inn pedo ke neeche, meri

Udaasi ko kalam mein, aur uski

Khayalo ko syaahi bana betha hun.

poems/kuch-lafz.html.title: Kuch Lafz
poems/kuch-lafz.html.subtitle: A ghazal of words that remain
poems/kuch-lafz.html.html:
I

Kuch lafz aaj bhi kisi ke naam reh gaye

Din ba din lafz kam safaat zyada beh gaye.

◆
II

Yun patjhad tanhai mein guzaarke

Hum sardi ka hausla badhaate gaye.

◆
III

Aaj gulshan se guzarte hue ek khayal aya

Kuch khayal jo raat ko sataake subha chale gaye.

◆
IV

Tere gham ko jaan ki talaash thi

Talaash mein hum gham-o-jaan ho gaye.

◆
V

Jab gham ke waje khatm hote rahe

Tab tumhari yaadein wapis aake theher se gaye.

◆
VI

Aisi bhi kya bekhudi hai Raahi

Itna bebas fir ek bahaar ke liye ho gaye.

poems/lost-at-sea.html.title: Lost at Sea
poems/lost-at-sea.html.subtitle: The helmsman's grief.
poems/lost-at-sea.html.html:
I

Lost at sea,

the horizon as the captain's destination

a memory in his mind starts to flee

reminding him of a time when he was free from his desolation.

◆
II

Even with burdens on their shoulders

the passengers seem to smile freely

yet a misery resides on their fingers

while the helmsman steers through the waves cautiously.

◆
III

Ponders the yachtsman with a heart that is heavy

and a soul that can never be free

from all the times he drinks in misery

and the times when this heart was his own and once, so was she.

◆
IV

With an aching in their heart

the dockers dance in the early mornin rain

the seafarer watches on, near a pillar that is scarred

and with eyes that reflect his long lost pain.

◆
V

The old salt remembers a place where the liquor tasted good

now, in the sea, it tastes of his guilt, anger

and a depression that he has withstood

while he searches for a rope that feels rougher.

◆
VI

This old boat gets the bosun down, it makes him suffer

as a rush of distasteful memories come to his mind

pushing him to his limits and making him tougher

all he does is cling on to a hope, a hope that one day he could go see his child.

◆
VII

The ferryman feels stuck on this boat

feeling cold, drunk and lethargic

he rows with a might that lets it stay afloat

and now only God could bring him hope.

◆
VIII

Somedays a blue mist surrounds the sailor's soul

he wonders when his heart would be free

from the sorrow that makes him whole

and from the apathy that binds his heart from being carefree.

◆
IX

At the end of the sea

the cap'n stops searching for a purpose or a destination

he realises that he can't see

the horizon that he once felt was his salvation.

◆
X

The company grasp their life's lonely tale

as they come to understand

that life is all about the journey in detail

rather than its destination, that once had made them leave their homeland.

poems/my-dear-melancholy.html.title: My Dear Melancholy
poems/my-dear-melancholy.html.subtitle: A dialogue with sorrow itself
poems/my-dear-melancholy.html.html:
I

O my dear melancholy

You just took her face

Caressing the green grass

You have arrived so late.

◆
II

The old letters make me ponder

If the pen writes through its own will

Slipping emotions through a finger

Putting me in a saddening bliss.

◆
III

In a quiet tide of ignorance

A past joy that was fleeting

Now weighs down heavily

On my cigarette that keeps breaking.

◆
IV

I shadow the joy that seeps

Through the merry day

Wanting to touch me heaps

But, you, never let it find a way.

◆
V

You quietly dissect every feud

Carving your way with glee

And I never end up finding what I need

But you find your way to me.

◆
VI

O my dear melancholy

How much have I missed you?

O my dear melancholy

When will I forsake you?

poems/naya-rang.html.title: Naya Rang
poems/naya-rang.html.subtitle: A new colour fills the heart's shadow.
poems/naya-rang.html.html:
I

Aaj koi nayi kala dekhne ko mili hai

Kese kahe unki taraf aankhe bhatakne ko lagi hai.

◆
II

Unki justuju mein doob jaane ko mann hai

Ye bandagi koi nayi to nahi hai.

◆
III

Junoon mein aise khone ka shauq kabhi tha nahi

Fir aaj kyon unke husn ka junoon mujhpe sawaar hai.

◆
IV

Unki chandni baahein jo sama rang de

Ab mere dil ke saaye mein bhi rang bhar raha hai.

◆
V

Meri aankhe unko takte takte nahi thaki

Kher aankhe to sirf dil ka kehna maan rahi hai.

◆
VI

Unki ada mere pannon mein sama jaaye

Iss muddat ki ye hi khwaish hai.

poems/once-again.html.title: Once Again
poems/once-again.html.subtitle: The cyclical nature of longing.
poems/once-again.html.html:
I

Once again,

the regrets keep burdening my shoulder

while the melodies which once offered me joy

now remind me of a pain that tries to linger

and of a sorrow that this pen does enjoy.

◆
II

One more time,

I wanted myself to stay

but my mind advised constraint

as my tears no longer lay

in wait for her, while my eyes can only refrain.

◆
III

How can I erase these,

memories that only bring tears

of sorrow and benign

and will continue for years

unless I heal this broken heart of mine.

◆
IV

One last time,

I want to see her somewhere

at the same old coffee house that still is plain

in a bookstore, reading the sonnets of yesteryear

or in a shade, staying away from rain.

◆
V

And in those moments,

will I be able to find closure?

over this love that is deemed to be hopeless

will my words of love reach her?

that fill my poems, yet, feel wordless.

◆
VI

Once again,

my conscience threatens to be horrified

as it seems that these words might fall short

before reaching her, while I abide

to a twist of fate, that will retort.

◆
VII

I wait for the day,

when this mind may numb this pain

that comes and goes in pieces that stray

as only the memories remain

while I hope that the sorrow slowly fades away.

◆
VIII

These poems stare at me for hours,

I write these poems for her

or for a woman that seems to be her

to read these poems, is all I want from her

while I wait for a reply from her.

 

Once again I wait,

for a woman to walk into this room

in my heart that has long been closed

and I smoke a cigarette in wait, that doesn't seem to be a boon

while the dying embers of this cigarette that has dozed

and of my love,

 

fall on this poem.

poems/once-more.html.title: Once More
poems/once-more.html.subtitle: On love that returns to haunt.
poems/once-more.html.html:
I

I had forgotten her voice and face,

but now I can see her in the flower in my vase.

Now she messages me again,

making me reminisce the love I had to refrain.

◆
II

The serenity in her voice and eyes,

yet again brings me to my knees at sunrise.

She showers her signs of sympathy upon me,

feels like an utter and unjust misery.

◆
III

When my hands had just found peace,

she comes again to rattle my sleep.

My hands have started wandering again,

towards a pen that writes down my pain.

◆
IV

Now I write down a poem about a tale,

that seems to her like a funny charade.

Golden slumbers fill her eyes and dry mine,

a sorrow that befalls on my words, on this line.

◆
V

I was on a hiatus from this suffering,

now she returns with a smile that seems to be a good way of covering.

But this heart knows that it's a comedy,

for my soul knows about her apathy.

I had met her and that was fate's twist,

but now, she comes back with a cynical fit.

I write beside a window on a rainy day,

and these words strain to rhyme yet, I pray.

◆

Now I move on with my life as I did before,

without any concrete purpose anymore.

I must keep on writing poems about her and someone like her,

until I find the words to this incomplete poem,

that lies ahead on this long and winding road.

poems/only-the-garden-roses.html.title: Only the Garden Roses Were Listening
poems/only-the-garden-roses.html.subtitle: A secret kept by the garden.
poems/only-the-garden-roses.html.html:
I

A day of autumn laden with flowers

is accompanied by a sorrowful night

hampered with scattering tears

in echoes of old memories in plight.

◆
II

A hopeful afternoon is spent in a bus

sightseeing and travelling around the city,

while emotions crash on a dubious

humming tune that remains blue and weary.

◆
III

I sauntered under the autumn sky

in search for an October's wish

that would reverse a day of July,

a day when she left in anguish.

◆
IV

I strolled empty streets in the evening

I looked upon a tree with orange leaves

that made me reminisce a wandering

woman whose beauty could rival a lily.

◆
V

Seasons ago we met without a choice,

my voice sounded like the rusting

leaves in front of her enigmatic voice,

that was calm even when it was raining.

◆
VI

She told me to not be so mysterious

as we dawdled through a garden

I wondered if she really knew

my love for her, hidden in my heart's den.

 

Only the garden roses were listening

she whispered near the garden of lily,

I wondered if fate was recurring

or hinting me of another misery.

◆
VII

Seasons felt like days with her

but now, without her, it's an eternal

autumn of sorrow in October

when even a new love is fatal.

◆
VIII

I boarded a nostalgic train back,

but these memories come and go

in this benign yet regretful month

where only bittersweet memories flow.

poems/painting-her.html.title: Painting Her
poems/painting-her.html.subtitle: She smiled over a novel while I drew her reflection on a wine bottle.
poems/painting-her.html.html:
I

A railroad rusted in no mystery

Is beside a small coffee house,

I try to paint a vivid scenery

Dusted by life without a spouse.

◆
II

In my quiet longing for the spring

I see a woman walk by in the rain

While flowers bloom in the morning

That were withered for long in pain.

◆
III

The winds of the rain dance

Around her which reminds me

Of a sparkling coast in Barcelona

Where the sun is calm as the sea.

◆
IV

Sipping the coffee while reading

An obscure romance novel,

She smiles while I keep painting

Her reflection I see on a wine bottle.

◆
V

Losing track of weather & season

I bide my time for a new artistry,

To draw her eyes for no reason

On my canvas under an oak tree.

◆
VI

When the evening comes in haste

I smoke a cigarette of mint

And like the clouds in Autumn

She disappears without a hint.

◆
VII

As the days of snow approached

She stopped visiting this place,

Making the memories a facade

And turning my art into a daze.

◆
VIII

A painting with a lonely memory

Is on my canvas as if it was a fantasy.

It's an art that awaits a melody

Which danced around her beauty.

◆
IX

The season of spring nears me

And my loneliness is on a spree

Of painting her reminiscent imagery

That is etched into my heart for eternity.

poems/patjhad-ka-parichay.html.title: Patjhad Ka Parichay
poems/patjhad-ka-parichay.html.subtitle: How autumn introduces itself.
poems/patjhad-ka-parichay.html.html:
I

Aaj ye thandi hawa apna

Parichaya karta hai mujhse

Aur mere kalam se jo dikhata hai

Khwab mere dil ko iss suhani raat.

◆
II

Chaudavi ka chandh iss sanjh

Rachta hai har shayar ke liye

Aisi saajish jo karde shahad

Ki mukhi ko bhi sharminda.

◆
III

Beheka bahar hi jaanta hai jo

Mujhe mila gaya tha ik shayar

Ke khwab se jisne mere

Mohabbat ki dastaan palat di.

◆
IV

Taras gaye hai meri aankhein

Ab uss haseena ko dekhne mein

Jo mere khwab mein aakar meri

Nazm mein shaamil ho gayi.

◆
V

Ab manzil reh gaye hai anjaan

Jo kuch mausam pehle the

Jankaar, aur awaara reh gaya

Hai ye dil, jo tha pehele samajhdar.

◆
VI

Kagazo mein uski taareef

Barkaraar hai aur iss chandni

Raat ko wo leti hai tashrif

Mere dil ki suhaani kavita mein.

◆
VII

Mile the hum ik chhote mod pe

Jo tha khila bahaar ke phoolo

Se, par ab wo sadak mein sirf

Reh gaye, murjhaye hue phool.

◆
VIII

Dil jalati thi wo mera, apni

Yaari sabke liye dikhake

Mein haath malte reh gaya

Aur shaamein dhalte gaye.

◆
IX

Ik baar phirse ban gaye

Hum dono ishq mein ajnabi

Jab pata chala mujhe ki uski

Kashmo kashm mein tha anjaana.

◆
X

Lakh haseen dekhe the

Par ussa nahi dekha tha

Ab bas hai wo shayar ka khwab

Aur ek kavi ki bahar-e-mehboob.

◆
XI

Iss raat pedo ki shaakho pe aisi

Khamoshi chhayi jo use yaad

Karne mein karta hai majboor

Aur uski yaadein na hoti riha.

◆
XII

Kuch palo ka hai ye guztaakh sama

Kabhi ho payegi wo mujhse juda?

Bas lotkar na aye kaafile bahar ke

Chalo firse banaya ajnabi zindagi ne.

poems/pehele-aur-fir.html.title: Pehele Aur Fir
poems/pehele-aur-fir.html.subtitle: First one thing, then another
poems/pehele-aur-fir.html.html:
I

Unki hasi jo bahaaron ke phool sajade

Mujhe pehele aashiqi, fir maayusi, aur fir tanhai mein dhakel gaye.

◆
II

Chup chupke unhe dekhaa karte the,

Dekhte dekhte pehele dilkash, fir aashiq aur fir shayar ban gaye.

◆
III

Aap to nazdeek se bhi kitne jhut bolte rahe

Pehele ek baar, fir do baar, fir kayi baar dil tod gaye.

◆
IV

Din ba din badhti gayi, iss zindagi ke zulm hum pe

Pehele gulshan, fir gul-badan, fir gul murjhake jhad gaye.

◆
V

Haule haule unke saare taqaluff mit gaye

Aap se, phir tum hue, fir tum ke baad tum kaun ho gaye.

◆
VI

Aisa tha kya unke andaaz mein

Jo pehele, mann mein, fir soch mein aur fir panno mein sama gaye.

poems/red-sweater.html.title: Red Sweater
poems/red-sweater.html.subtitle: Written under the shade of a garden
poems/red-sweater.html.html:
I

The sun shines less than usual

Like a lost love finding itself in a gravel,

The fallen leaves do not appear as lovely

An autumn's sign for travel.

◆
II

I sit under the shade of this garden

Penning my thoughts down that take shape

Of poetry that remains too brazen

For my heart has lost an escape.

◆
III

A sudden gush of wind flows past my book

Flowers of the garden dance to its tune

While I smoke away my feelings that shook

Me and my poetry on a fateful day of June.

◆
IV

Thoughts become fleeting under this tree

Memories that once sparked an ember

In my heart still lurks in my poetry

Keeping me warm in this lonely winter.

◆
V

She often wore a red sweater,

Calling me when she wanted attention

Texting me to get her man under the weather

Making me join my own pitiful convention.

◆
VI

The birds fly from one place to another

Reminding me her words of that night

When she cried a river, and now I ponder

With all the time that has passed by, will she think of me tonight?

◆
VII

My friends tell me to quit smoking

But it's these memories that haunt my fingers

Which grips the cigarette, burning

The sorrows inside my heart that to this day, lingers.

◆
VIII

Like a cigarette that breaks in the rain

I break my heart every time I see this deluge

It hides my seemingly shallow pain

And under this shade my pen takes a silent refuge.

poems/regret.html.title: Regret
poems/regret.html.subtitle: The things I should have known.
poems/regret.html.html:
I

If I had known he wouldn't laugh with me again,

I'd have held him once more — before the rain.

◆
II

If I hadn't taken him for granted,

I might have heard the quiet he hid from everyone.

◆
III

If I had understood that her kindness wasn't love,

I wouldn't have fallen so far into it.

◆
IV

If I had known this regret would arrive,

I'd have spoken. Just once, out loud.

◆
V

If my mind hadn't turned against me first,

I might have forgiven the losses before they settled.

◆
VI

If I had seen what her eyes were asking,

she wouldn't be something I still write around.

◆
VII

Long ago, I chose to feel everything too deeply.

I've seen, since then, things this mind can't unlearn.

◆
VIII

If I had known there was always a boat to solitude,

I would have gone quietly

instead of fighting every current home.

◆
IX

If I had known that betrayal was just

the shape a life takes —

I would have found a gentler way to let this one go.

poems/saboot.html.title: Saboot
poems/saboot.html.subtitle: Proof. A classical ghazal form.
poems/saboot.html.html:
Raat bhar tumhari yaad se ghire hi to hai

Us yaad mein shamm-e-gham jalaya hi to hai.

Chala tha zikr bewafai ka inn baharo mein

So tumhara khayal aya magar bhulana hi to hai.

Tumse baat hue ek zamaana hua magar

Us hasi ko ojhal hona abhi baaki hi to hai.

Hum par be-dilli ka ilzaam hi to hai

Iqrar hi sahi muhabbat azaab hi to hai.

Koi jurm to nahi tumse anjaan-e-ishq karna

Tumhara hum pe waqt guzarna aziyat hi to hai.

Kitna be-bas karega ab ye teri-meri chuppi

Jaan-e-jaan ye ghazal mein tera naam hi to hai.

Tera khil jana mujhse baat karke sachai hi to hai

Tera yun baat talna har baat pe haan hi to hai.

Ab inn hothon pe naam tera to nahi

Fir bhi bahare tera pata dhundte hi to hai.

Kitne hi dil-farebi reh jao tum 'Raahi'

Ye ghazal saboot hai ki ye pyaar hi to hai.

poems/sardi-ka-mahina.html.title: Sardi Ka Mahina
poems/sardi-ka-mahina.html.subtitle: A month that returns with its memories.
poems/sardi-ka-mahina.html.html:
Sardi mein hi yaadein karti hai wapsi

Jo uss rahguzar mein kho gaye the shayad.

Aankhon ki mukhbiri ne kuch baatein kahi thi

To wo jaan hi gaya hoga hume unse pyar hai shayad.

Hazaar baar unse guftugu hui thi lekin

Hazaar baar kuch baat reh gayi thi shayad.

Lagta nahi ke patjhad ko humse koi gila hai

Par patton ki tarah hum to akele reh gaye shayad.

Naye gulon se jaan-pehechaan kaha hogi

Ae dil, unn zulfon ko tu bhula nahi shayad.

Zindagi bhar na bhulunga iss gham ko

Anjaam-e-aashiqi ka anjaam hi hai shayad.

Hum tauba karke mar gaye the be-maut

Tumhare aankhon ki maikashi thi shayad.

Jisse bichhda hai ab use bhul jaa Raahi

Uske khat uska intezar karte honge shayad.

Aaj fir usi rahguzar par khada hun

Jo kuch mausam pehele nakara tha shayad.

poems/september.html.title: September
poems/september.html.subtitle: A month that never intends to stay.
poems/september.html.html:
I

She was a woman of my dreams

who was like the ending of summer

and now I have wasted years

in pursuit of forgetting her.

◆
II

A woman who appeared in a storm

came and instilled a calmness

that I couldn't have asked as my norm

yet, it's all I could ask in a tone, reckless.

◆
III

She was a woman who brought spring

into my rain and sorrow filled life

but she disappeared in the wind

just when my love had come alive.

◆
IV

She was a woman whose smile

had become my heart's desire

and as I dreamt her on an aisle

she faded and made my life a satire.

◆
V

She seldom made me question

my sentimental approach to destiny

now all I do is smile in tandem

with the poems I write in mockery.

◆
VI

Her hands so warm and kind

played the piano in the key of C

that brought solace to my mind

while I wrote a haiku that got lost in sea.

◆
VII

She brought a change in me for good

while I wanted to be close to her

yet I could never get the chance

as she always had him beside her.

◆
VIII

Perhaps she's the only reason

why I write this sorrowful poem

however, loving her maybe my treason

as I have forgotten the song she did hum.

◆
IX

Maybe the reason I write this song

is a way of avenging my grief

but her memory does prolong

a sorrow that I have hid in this leaf.

◆
X

Now as I sit on this park bench

I reminisce a time of August

poems/shaam-e-gham.html.title: Shaam-e-Gham
poems/shaam-e-gham.html.subtitle: Sorrow of the Evening
poems/shaam-e-gham.html.html:
Mujhe har waqt yaad aata hai

Ke maine tumhe bhula diya.

Baarish ke boond sawaal karte hai

Jawaab jinke lafzon ne daba diya.

Mayusi theher gayi hai dil mein

Aisi bekhudi ka sabab hawa mein uda diya.

Meri har koshish ishq ki nakaam hi rahi

Itna tajurba lekar bhi khud ko hara diya.

Meri zillat safar karegi aur kuch door

Ek nadi kinare iss khat ka naav bana diya.

Tum jao aur dariya dariya pyaas bhujao

Ab kisi aur ke dil ko samjhota karao.

Hume bhi shauq na tha dastaan sunane ka

Taqalluf mein usne to aise hi puch diya.

Pyaar se 'Raahi' bulaake taqalluf mein daal diya

Ye dil jo toot gaya use naam se bulaake fir jaga diya.

poems/shayad.html.subtitle: A ghazal of perhaps
poems/shayad.html.html:
I

Likhe the khat khwaabon mein bhi tumhe

Ek nazm tumhe aur dikhana hai shayad.

◆
II

Sher-o-shayari karte rahe sheher sheher

Ab bhi yaadein baaki reh gayi shayad.

◆
III

Tumhari kitaabe jhaankti hai almaari se

Unko na padhne mein hi bhalai hai shayad.

◆
IV

Ye qalam dhunta hai fir nayi si bedili ko

Mujhse ek naya paigam likhwayega shayad.

◆
V

Bebasi hai par ankahi chuban si hai,

Bade sheher mein ab ghutan si hai shayad.

◆
VI

Tumhari gali se guzre to aankhe bhar aayi

Tumhe bhulaane mein abhi aur waqt lagega shayad.

◆
VII

Khaas hum bhi the kisi ki nazron mein Raahi,

Magar nazar ki khwaishein badalne mein waqt nahi laga shayad.

◆
VIII

Gale lagna ho muhabbat ko to abhi lage

Der ho gayi to uske bagair jee lagne lagega shayad.

poems/simple-twist-of-fate.html.title: Simple Twist of Fate
poems/simple-twist-of-fate.html.subtitle: Wild strawberry fields and a missed bus.
poems/simple-twist-of-fate.html.html:
I

Half drunk and completely hopeless,

I keep chiming on this typewriter

while a hummingbird hums melancholy

through these lonesome nights.

◆
II

The morning rises with a grief I can't name —

I only know it started the day I saw her smile

and mistook it for a door.

◆
III

I missed my bus on a lonesome rainy day.

Life changed with a simple twist of fate:

she was standing beside the wild strawberry fields

under that gloomy shade,

and I forgot where I was going.

◆
IV

I was guilty of daydreaming in her eyes,

in the little details of her life,

while time slipped through without asking.

Now even the clock is unbearable —

it only shows how slowly things move

when you are waiting for nothing.

◆
V

She showed me winter could have colour.

She was proof that autumn could break your heart

while still being beautiful.

 

I wonder if I'll find her again —

near the garden full of lilies,

at the old bookstore,

or under an umbrella.

◆
VI

The words still fall on this page,

and I keep writing,

half drunk,

completely hopeless,

waiting one more time

for a simple twist of fate.

poems/tale-of-wandering-poet.html.title: Tale of the Wandering Poet
poems/tale-of-wandering-poet.html.subtitle: A meditation on versions and transformation
poems/tale-of-wandering-poet.html.html:
I

Which version is it?

I can't seem to find you in my poetry anymore.

Is it you or someone else?

In the years that I knew you,

now more years went past loving you.

Can I count it on my hand,

or the pages of poetry

that have you as a "her"

who just slips past as thoughts

from my heart through my fingers

into my diary's fading ink?

◆
II

Now, with your mention in its stead,

the page seems complete yet haunted

of the old memories that I let go.

But it does come back,

coming through the faint cracks

that slowly close as time passes by.

◆
III

Which version are you now,

that has bled into my heart today?

Which version are you tomorrow,

that sleeps silently as I prattle

about my life that is without worries?

◆
IV

Which version would you be

when I love someone again?

I am confident that this love,

that I used to feel for you,

will only make me feel even stronger

for the destined woman

that I have been waiting

for the past few lifetimes.

◆
V

Which version would you be, my destiny?

I await your soft advent into my heart

to win it without contention.

◆
VI

Which version am I?

Living as a wandering poet,

believing, as I walk away from yesterday.

poems/the-bar-under-a-lonely-star.html.title: The Bar Under a Lonely Star
poems/the-bar-under-a-lonely-star.html.subtitle: Only broken people gathered there — just to get a sip of whiskey & lime.
poems/the-bar-under-a-lonely-star.html.html:
I

I stumbled upon a secluded bar

One breezy & windy December day.

It was situated under a lonely star

But, was filled with people anyway.

◆
II

Here only broken people gathered

Just to get a sip of whiskey & lime

That has long since been withered

On these long days with no sunshine.

◆
III

I entered with no specific objective

But this peculiar place was on its own

Tied to a premise in an anxious subjective

Tone, only to get hopelessly drunk alone.

◆
IV

A gloomy shadow looms over

An old man's scar filled face,

A face that hadn't come to lower

Its pride which now, seems a charade.

◆
V

A semi shattered vinyl player

Grinds through the gloomy night

And the lonesome could only savour

A sharp tonic with a lonesome plight.

◆
VI

Wistful smiles popped on the buzzed

As a specific melody reminded them

Of a time when the heart wasn't puzzled,

And of a time when life was a poem.

◆
VII

A trumpet blares through the shade

Stirring a melancholic sensation

And the piano artfully lets the pain fade

While it dissolves in the mind's ocean.

◆
VIII

The sounds of distant glasses clink

Carried by a sadness stuck on their face

Made my empty and horrid heart sink

In misery as a dire mockery was in place.

◆
IX

And as I sit down by this lonely lady

Whose main motive in life was only to

Measure her costly glass of brandy

At the bar where the bill stayed due.

◆
X

My gutted face enveloped in sorrow

My pale and dry lips subtly drown

In the glass of whiskey too shallow

While my hands tremble to a sound.

◆
XI

A sound of a woman who is beside me,

Forcing me to hopelessly remember

A time with a woman who was like a maple tree,

Who blew away with the winds of December.

◆
XII

This woman beside me was dressed in blue,

And tried to see the scribbling in my diary

But a cold wind came in and hastily blew

Away the poems that described a canary.

◆
XIII

Before midnight, I exited from this bar

Which almost made me its abductee.

Now in the night sky, I see a lonely star

That others inside the bar couldn't see.

◆
XIV

I light up a cigarette as I stand below

A streetlight that illuminates the dark

Streets of this town covered in snow

And the rain while I decide to embark,

◆
XV

On a journey to find the correct word

To complete this rigid poem of mine.

I smoke while I mark a grave for a bird

Which lied inside my lonely & rusty heart.

◆
XVI

It died without seeing a ray of sunshine

That escapes from my diary, but I can't save

These poems in my diary forever, that act as light

For the flowers to bloom at my isolated grave.

◆
XVII

Time has hurried on, as I kept on writing

These miserable poems, that have me and her.

 

While she blew away with the cold winds

Of December, that have now, run full circle.
