poems/the-blue-scarf.html.title: The Blue Scarf
poems/the-blue-scarf.html.subtitle: She worked at a bookshop that played music for wanderers.
poems/the-blue-scarf.html.html:
I

A wry memory alludes my mind

As I think about a straining rhyme

For a poem that is hard to write

While the world changes with time.

◆
II

Opposite to the bus stop's street

Was a bookshop laden with lily

And juniper that formed a sweet

Scenery in order with the reality.

◆
III

The shade of this old bus stop

Misses the serene glimpses of her,

Who worked at an artful bookshop

Which played music for the wanderer.

◆
IV

I used to wait for my bus on a floor

Until I noticed flowers that wither,

Through the window of that store

Which are still there, except her.

◆
V

She had a pashmina for the winter

And a light blue scarf to cover her

Hair that would make even summer

Shy & wary until it's September.

◆
VI

Her long hair flowed with the winds

That were chilly & cold in October

While the enigma of her red heels

Made me feel in peace, like a river.

◆
VII

I met her on a fateful rainy day

In this stop's magnanimous shade

As her eyes made my thoughts stray

While I hid my emotions in charade.

◆
VIII

It seemed as if she could clearly see

The wicked world & its foolish ways

From eyes that were blue like the sea

Yet I write a verse that only fakes.

◆
IX

It's been many seasons since I saw

Her in that empty book store

Which without her, is like a flaw

And the music fades with no flow.

◆
X

Therefore all I do is keep her

Alive in my melancholic memory,

As we met in the shade of a September

Who now lives on through my poetry.

poems/the-gardner.html.title: The Gardner
poems/the-gardner.html.subtitle: Seasons passed. She kept coming. He never forgot.
poems/the-gardner.html.html:
I

A Gardner, lonely as he could be

Works at a garden in the city

Where flowers crave to be free

From the despondent calamity.

◆
II

A calamity that showers rain

Full of sorrow and regret

That causes a nostalgic pain

That he can never seem to forget.

◆
III

He observes the world changing,

But his pain that seems sweet

Abides, & also does the clinking

Of glass windows from the street.

◆
IV

He often notices the woman

Who lives in that old house

Where the glass clinks during dawn

And its a place without a spouse.

◆
V

Time and again she comes by

The garden for a flower lily,

Blooming in peace and solitary

And as sun dawns, she bids goodbye.

◆
VI

Her eyes looked in the garden

For something far ahead in life

That made him write a poem

About a woman who wasn't a wife.

◆
VII

In summer time, the woman

Would wear dark sunglasses

That didn't let any human

See her exuberant face.

◆
VIII

Spring season was their favourite

As she could see more beauty

In the garden while the literate

Gardener could do his duty.

◆
IX

On a rainy day, she would quietly

Stand with a blue umbrella,

Beside the flowers in the vicinity

While raindrops fell on his viyella.

◆
X

In autumn she would look

At the brown leaves that fall

While she clenched a book

With her hands that seemed small.

◆
XI

During winter, she would wear

A trench coat that was brown

And visit the garden lair

& In sorrow, they both would drown.

◆
XII

Numerous seasons passed

While she kept coming to the garden

For the flowers that weren't recast

As the man had never forgotten.

 & In sorrow, they both would drown.

 Numerous seasons passed

poems/the-green-umbrella.html.title: The Green Umbrella
poems/the-green-umbrella.html.subtitle: She walked away under the umbrella I had given her.
poems/the-green-umbrella.html.html:
I

It's a lonely month of June

A windless summer time

I write with no rhythm or tune

As no rainy days are in sight.

◆
II

But this season ushered

A sudden rain in delight

In the heart that shattered

Several seasons ago in plight.

◆
III

This night chooses a dream

That was serene in my eyes,

How could I ever forget that smile

That resembled a night without lies.

◆
IV

I saw her near the old bus stop

Searching shelter from the rain,

I was beside the dusty shop

Soaking in a nostalgic pain.

◆
V

I gave her the green umbrella

Which she once had gifted me.

Now she grips the same Viyella

With a face full of glee.

◆
VI

As she walked beside me

The rainswept streets fell silent

And the winds played a memory

Which made my heart heavy.

◆
VII

I saw a ring on her finger

As she was picking a lily,

I felt a sorrow that will linger

In my poems of chivalry.

◆
VIII

Her hair reflected the moonlight

When she caught the bus in a hurry,

We bid an emotionless goodbye

While the night became hazy.

◆
IX

Now it's the month of July

The night chooses a dream

Where an old love chose to fly

But I kept mine, in a poem.

poems/the-longer-route.html.title: The Longer Route
poems/the-longer-route.html.subtitle: A walk through memory, identity, and the self we carry home
poems/the-longer-route.html.html:
I

I take a longer route as I walk

Past the street that I had forgotten

Laden with flowers it awaits

My treacherous mind's silence.

◆
II

Unspoken words seldom spill out

As tears that trickle down slow

Weighing a life's worth of sorrow

That will guide me astray tomorrow

◆
III

Smiling my way through old memories

That were left in upon my almira

It is a wonder that the delusion

Kept itself going without confusion.

◆
IV

Is it a memory or a longing —

The grassland, the sunflowers, and the blue sky

A child running through yellow light

Or a life I haven't lived into

◆
V

The mind plays its film without asking

My eyes well up and they look away

While I close the almira, call it nothing

Only to weep without warning one day

◆
VI

I wore the face that I led myself into

And somewhere lost the one beneath

My poetry bleeds at every turn now

For the self that got lost in time

◆
VII

Will she too see only what I've shown

And love a face who I've long outgrown

Or will she find what I haven't yet

A self I cannot remember or own

◆
VIII

Gradually, I remember the tears

The heart that withered at a friend's death

Lifetime worth of non validated memories

What is true and what is false anymore.

◆
IX

Various melodies arrive in a tongue I knew,

A Spiritual tune, another with my mother's voice

Another which reminisced in a love that left,

Or a tune for a love not yet born

◆
X

It carried an immense longing I cannot place in time

Perhaps carried from a life before this

I do not know if I need to be held

Or if my arms are meant to hold instead

◆
XI

I am now tired of finding answers

Loneliness is not the cause of this state

When the heart does not have refuge

As the call for help was never a smile.

◆
XII

Seasons change with every turn

Of my poetry and its passages

As I look at the serene sunset with wonder

Of when it will all dawn on my heart, again.

◆
XIII

I take a longer route as I drive

Through the lush green nature

Where the fresh air makes me bribe

My wounded soul, guiding itself into solace.

poems/the-tattered-page.html.title: The Tattered Page
poems/the-tattered-page.html.subtitle: Written near a lake's shore, the night before the front.
poems/the-tattered-page.html.html:
I

A soldier writes on a tattered page,

A poem written near a lake's shore

That is outside the tents of shade,

As of tomorrow, he heads for war.

◆
II

It's a lonely & desperate cry for help

Under the starry filled night sky

He writes this poem on the things he felt

About the incidents he perceived in July

◆
III

On duty, so he may not forget reality.

◆
IV

He saw a fright in the eyes of a recruit

Rushing towards the sole bunker

Where resides a major who is a hoot,

A man who will follow death in a flutter.

◆
V

Hearts that had forgotten to slow down

Kept running in a dire & constant horror

As a bomb on the battlefield may drop down,

Adding more bodies to become fodder.

◆
VI

He saw a bunch of pilots meeting

Their families, the smiles were cut in

With tears of sorrow that were falling,

As of tomorrow, they are airborne therein.

◆
VII

He heard the story of the lieutenant

Who was in enemy land without a dorm,

A woman who lived near as a tenant

Gave him a shelter from the storm.

◆
VIII

The woman had silver bracelets

In her wrists & flowers in her hair

She died in his arms, as bullets fired in sets,

Now he has no heart for his own share.

◆
IX

He observes a deputy who had erupted

In anger at the sepoys who were afraid

Of the corpses which fate had decided,

And God had made flowers in facade.

◆
X

The soldier gets up the next day

He arms himself to feel a bit secure

While the army doesn't intend to delay,

As they join the frontlines to endure.

◆
XI

All of them were given a deadly boot

As everyone was killed in a dogfight.

He was wounded & wanted to shoot

Himself to be relieved of the spite.

◆
XII

As he was about to push the gun's trigger

He sights a thorny rose beside his feet

On a pool of blood that made him shiver,

He picked it & under a tree, he found a seat.

◆
XIII

A seat beside the pile of corpses

That were forming a haunting shadow.

Grief, misery & sorrow now courses

Through his veins that are now hollow.

◆
XIV

He had a lot of blood loss from the wound

In his arm, yet he hangs onto the rose

Firmly, while he also clutches the shroud

Of his comrade, who died without a repose.

◆
XV

The thorny rose stays with & by him

Until he breathes his last breath,

He wonders if someone read the poem

He wrote near that shore as now he is dead.

◆
XVI

He died under the lonely shade of a tree

While a wind blows, making the leaves fall

On his body, that once was on a kill spree,

As nature marks a grave for him, this fall.

◆
XVII

The battlefield had become a graveyard

Without anyone's name. Corpses lie in wait,

While a silent wind blows through the yard,

As it's September, a month that they hate.

poems/the-wardens-garden.html.title: The Warden's Garden
poems/the-wardens-garden.html.subtitle: He kept the garden. The garden kept him.
poems/the-wardens-garden.html.html:
I

A man with a horrific past

Had done unspeakable deeds

Now longs to find peace & be free

From those shackles of his creeds.

◆
II

He finds a work to escape from calamity

A place he could find the peace he craved

A place where people were like his family

A garden where his life felt paved.

◆
III

Spending his days by watering the garden

He thinks of himself as a lonely convict

And acts as a peaceful warden

While he smokes away his mind's verdict.

◆
IV

He meets a woman in that place

She was a maid, who carried a vase

And had a peculiar scar on her face

That reminded him of cruelty in solace.

◆
V

He gives sage advice to people around

Which he wished he had got in the past

While she stands in the corner of the room

With a smile that made him aghast.

◆
VI

He sits beside her on a rainy evening

As she knits him a glove for the winter

He looks at her eyes like the moon

And fears that he may fall in love with her.

◆
VII

A notice came from the army one evening

She opens the letter and gets tears

He finds out that he had been drafted

For the rest of his years.

◆
VIII

He had bought her a beautiful hair clip

Which he wanted to give her in repose

But now, he hides it in his room with a slip

Along with the feelings that he cannot disclose.

◆
IX

A wistful smile appears on his face

As he looks at what he leaves behind,

A room full of memories, a charming vase,

And people who were family to him.

◆
X

He heads to the station with only a bag full of memories

While the household cries in agony.

She grabs ahold of him just as he boards

Tears fall from her eyes in misery.

◆
XI

He wipes her tears, he asks her to marry

A nice man & wishes a good life to her.

No words of love were said in a hurry

As the eyes had already confessed, on one rainy September.

◆
XII

With a wry smile, he bids them farewell

The train departs, leaving only love

And solitude behind as fate could compel

He looks at her photo & could only dwell.

◆
XIII

He died in war, that was theirs to lose

And people left behind could just grieve

While a sorrow with an endless premise

Had landed on their heart's retrieve.

◆
XIV

She is now a Nana & has lived a happy life.

Now on her deathbed, she has only one regret,

She couldn't convey her feelings that night

To an old love that she could never forget.

◆
XV

She lost a love in this life's trip

While he just vanished in the wind

Leaving only that hair clip

And those lingering feelings behind,

◆
XVI

In that dusty room from ages ago

And the leaves that were green turn to brown.

poems/the-woman-who-brought-spring.html.title: The Woman Who Brought Spring
poems/the-woman-who-brought-spring.html.subtitle: She returned the season.
poems/the-woman-who-brought-spring.html.html:
I

I wandered in a garden full of marigold

It reminded me of a time that has flown

When romantic poetry was for the old

And for the people who were left alone.

◆
II

I saw a sage like alyssum flower

Hiding in beauty among others,

It resembled a girl I met in October

When leaves fall like feathers.

◆
III

These flowers that are not cherished

Wither and die like the autumn leaves

Which are colored in a lonely dismay

Waiting to turn callous and grey.

◆
IV

My wish to watch the crooked rain

Again with her by my side felt a fantasy.

And when droplets slid down this shade

I saw her again in all her beauty.

◆
V

She entered this shade by the flowers

And the birds sang the tale of her beauty

In a nostalgic & melancholic symphony

Which pierced the lines in my poetry.

◆
VI

She was a woman who I knew once

Her smile could even make a rose shy

A smile that made me fall in love

A love which was new but now is old.

◆
VII

The rain falling on this shade felt serene

But her nostalgic smile like the flowers

Seemed more calmer than the rain

Which fatefully made us meet again.

◆
VIII

Greetings were exchanged, like the day

We met in this garden seasons ago,

Now she smiles with a few wrinkles

And my words still stumble to flow.

◆
IX

I saw her kids stroll along the garden

A bittersweet sight for a rainy day

A wry smile appeared on the curtain

Of my heart that reflected on my face.

◆
X

She bid farewell as the rain subsided

Her kids walked under an umbrella

Which a long time ago, I had gifted,

And I was left longing for the rain again.

◆
XI

I sighed as a snowy winter had arrived

The chilly winds entered this shade

Bringing forth emotions this December

That put an end to the reminiscence of her.

◆
XII

A beautiful reminiscence that once

Was present in my heart for a lifetime

Now is left aside while I wander again

Without a purpose, writing down

◆
XIII

Poetry that does not have her in it,

And a mystery that eludes me

Seeps into my mind as I look down

To the snow swept streets

◆
XIV

Realising, that life in all its misery

Just goes on.

poems/tokyo.html.title: Tokyo
poems/tokyo.html.subtitle: Two strangers in a city that has no gleeful clue
poems/tokyo.html.html:
I

The red light shines brighter than usual

Suggesting a momentary stop.

The man looks for clues in the new city

An unknown place for poets to rot.

◆
II

Everything seems unsure and unheard

Most of his time is lost in translation.

He saunters through the streets

To find a bookstore, secluded from all the fabrication.

◆
III

He picks up a dusty novel that was light

As his old fashioned pack of cigarettes.

Reading a few pages of the old book

Reminds him of the thoughts that he cannot digest.

◆
IV

Sitting in the bar, surrounded by dim lights

He sips his whiskey and catches a glimpse or two,

Of a woman who wore herself a dress

Whose eyes read everything in the room and were blue.

◆
V

They somehow light up their cigarettes

And prattle about how they are lost

In this city which has no gleeful clue

About their sorrowful life, in short.

◆
VI

They roam the night in the streets of Tokyo

Finding moments of solace in clamour.

She dances like there's no tomorrow

And he just observes her undisputed glamour.

◆
VII

Now they lay on the insomniac bed

Talking about all the uncertainty

That looms over their confused heads

While time passes quickly which before felt like eternity.

◆
VIII

They sleep soundly after days

With all the emotions washing away.

He wakes up finding her gone

A sudden rush of loneliness comes his way.

◆
IX

He finds an earring on his night stand

Accompanied by a letter he reads,

Smiling wryly he packs his bags

And for the airport he calmly leaves.

◆
X

He sees the same novel again

In someone's arms as he drives the car,

He smokes his cigarette sighing bemusedly

While the red light turns green from afar.

poems/tumhari-yaadein.html.subtitle: Memories of You
poems/tumhari-yaadein.html.html:
I

यूँ मन की गहराई में लिखता हूँ

बातें जो बसा लेती हैं, तुम्हारी यादें

तुम्हारी खुशी, तुम्हारी हँसी

देख फिर लिखता हूँ मन की बातें, तुम्हारी यादें।

◆
II

वसंत जाते जाते

नया ऋतु दे गया

अब शरद ने भी पत्तों का सहारा लिया

और लिपट गई आज, तुम्हारी यादें।

लिपट गई आज, तुम्हारी यादें।

◆
III

आँखों से संकेत कर

बस जाती थी वो, फूलों की किताबों में

वाक्यों से जो न बोला जाए

वो छंद से समा जाए, वही है तुम्हारी यादें।

◆
IV

किसी पीपल के पेड़ के नीचे बैठकर

गहरी सोच में उलझती है तुम्हारी यादें

किसी बगीचे से गुज़रते देखूँ सूरजमुखी को

फिर उस गाँव के प्रेम को उभार लाती हैं, तुम्हारी यादें।

poems/udaasi-ka-itiraf.html.title: Udaasi Ka Itiraf
poems/udaasi-ka-itiraf.html.subtitle: A confession the heart makes only to itself.
poems/udaasi-ka-itiraf.html.html:
Ye musafir jaam se pehele nazar fere nahi

Hum shaam ko piye bina kahi nikle nahi.

Yuhin mausam ki ada dekh ke yaad aya

Iss qismat ka kabhi tha saath nahi.

Gayab ho jaate hai ye nazmein aangan se har shaam

Ab to apne tanhai ka bhi sahaara nahi.

Agar muhabbat fir hoti qismat mein likhi

To iss bahaar ka hota itna afsos nahi.

Gulshan ko kitna bhi paani daalo

Inn gulon ke fitrat mein titliyan nahi.

Ab bedilli kaha chhodegi mera sahaara

Uske liye intezar karna tak to chhoda nahi.

Dil chidiyon ki aawaaz parakh leta hai

Itne aziyat jhelne ke baad dil ab nadaan nahi.

Log taquluff ko bhi samajte hai ikhlas

Har koi haath milaane wala dost nahi.

Jheel ke bahaav mein beh jaate hai har raat

Hum dil se nikale hue log ek jagah tikte nahi.

Raat se pehele hote hum jaam ke paas

Subha se pehele chhodte hum saath gilaas ka nahi.

Agar tum mil bhi jaate to ye afsaana khatm hota nahi

Zindagi mein to naye afsaano ki koi kami nahi.

Aisi udaasi ab kaha milti hai Raahi,

Ab to maan lo tumhe isse nafrat nahi.
